notation.C_K(x): Frozen K-candidate pool for input x.
notation.s(c|x): Frozen learned proposal/ranking score; no legality authority.
notation.L(c,x): Frozen legality predicate from support/typed/task authority.
notation.J(c,x): Hidden outcome/reference diagnostic, unavailable during generation and legality.

arms.A1: argmax over C_K(x) by s(c|x), ignoring L.
arms.A3: argmax over {c in C_K(x): L(c,x)=1} by the same s(c|x); abstain if empty.

event_estimands.rescue: 1[A1 illegal AND legal-set nonempty]. On every rescue, A3 changes output by construction.
event_estimands.dormant: 1[A1 legal]. A3 equals A1 by construction when the top-ranked candidate is legal.
event_estimands.hard_authority_violation_A3: Identically zero if implementation matches constitution; regression/nonzero value is a compiler failure.

aggregate.task_proxy_delta: J(A3)-J(A1), reported diagnostically and never used to redefine L post hoc

causal_identification: A1 and A3 share byte-identical C_K(x).
A1 and A3 share identical learned score s.
Therefore A1↔A3 output divergence identifies the local effect of the frozen legality gate conditional on the sampled candidate pool.
limitations: This is candidate-pool-conditional, not a claim over the full generator distribution.
A legal-set error can overconstrain valid language; monotonic safety applies to authority violations only if L is valid.
No output-quality theorem follows from rescue alone.
